2. Bermuda High will gradually give way over the new week

.DISCUSSION...
As of 210 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Another pleasant day is expected across the region today 
as high pressure continues to bring a period of drier weather. High 
temperatures will be a few degrees warmer today under light 
southerly flow with daytime highs climbing into the 80s areawide. 

Heading into the latter half of the week, warm and unsettled weather 
is expected as the region remains sandwiched between high pressure 
to the south and an upper level trough to the north, with zonal flow 
bringing several different disturbances to the region. With broad 
southwesterly flow ushering in plenty of moisture, chances for 
showers and thunderstorms will be possible. While there doesn't look 
to be any real defined boundary to help drive shower activity, the 
shortwave activity Thursday and Friday may provide enough energy to 
drive afternoon shower and thunderstorm chances. If ingredients 
align, there could be the potential for some stronger thunderstorms 
both afternoons, but generally more garden-variety thunderstorms can 
be expected. Shower activity is expected to wane towards the 
evenings with loss of diurnal heating. High temperatures Thursday 
will rise into the mid to upper 80s with dewpoints around 70 
degrees, resulting in heat indices in the upper 80s to around 90.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A Bermuda High will be remain in place Sunday through 
Tuesday, which will keep warm, moist flow progressing into the 
region while various systems travel west-to-east in quick zonal flow 
aloft. A more appreciable trough will drive southeastwards on 
Tuesday, and that will break down the Bermuda High and shunt the 
plume of moisture south and east of our region. Some forecast 
guidance still suggests there's a pocket of dry air in there 
somewhere between systems on Sunday, but the timing of this still 
remains a little uncertain. Any potential for stronger storms will 
depend on the time of day that these periodic 700mb troughs push 
east. If they are timed during peak heating, the warm, moist 
environment and gradually increasing shear suggests the ingredients 
could briefly materialize. Some of the experimental machine learning 
ensembles have some low end probabilities, but a greater focus 
south. So will keep an eye out, but any potential for stronger 
storms will be contingent on the timing of synoptic forcing. After 
Tuesday, we'll be under the influence of a broad upper low, bringing 
temperatures near to just below normal. However, there's still 
several embedded systems. So showers could remain in the forecast 
mid to late next week, but thunderstorm chances will minimize.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 12Z Thursday...Fog is expected to thin, with VFR
conditions and southwest winds 4-8 knots developing about 13-15z,
except at 7-10 knot lake breeze at KPBG. A few fair weather
cumulus clouds are possible, and some high clouds will start 
moving in from the south late in the day or beyond 00z Thursday.

Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
